$comment: Per-exam authoring contract, declared at S3 (exam-author, 2026-08-18) per methodology/02-master-inventory.md#siblings and methodology/03-authoring-guide.md#themes. Themes F1-F8 are DECLARED FRESH for this exam, not inherited: the T1-T8 architecture starter set assumes a design-decision exam, and AI-901 is a two-area exam whose majority area is implementation, so the judgment types had to be re-derived from the objective verbs (Describe/Identify on one side; Create, Deploy, Build, Implement, Respond to, Extract, Interpret on the other). theme_definitions carries the one-line judgment each theme exercises. pattern_extensions E01-E12 are the Microsoft vendor-extension registry defined in derivation/source-akashp-ai901-simulator.md#pattern-registry — E01-E08 reused unchanged from the AI-900 build so caps stay comparable across the vendor's exams, E09-E12 new for this exam's implementation half; caps live in manifest.validation.pattern_caps. AUTHORING EMPHASES the artefacts oblige S4 to apply: RAISE E05 granularity-slip (the best-made pattern in the accessible source and the one that maps onto the four text techniques, the vision task taxonomy and OCR-vs-field-extraction); ADOPT E11 agentic-tier-slip as a first-class pattern (the discrimination this exam is built on, used in only 6 of 196 source items); use E12 pipeline-stage-swap wherever a build order exists; keep E10 sdk-symbol-swap legitimate ONLY where the item turns on what code DOES, never on recalling a symbol. And the standing negative rule from the vocabulary-drift register: never key an item on a rename — a superseded service name may appear as a distractor, but no item may be answerable only by knowing that a product was renamed. Verticals are authored fresh at S3 as settings for AI work; none is copied from a source scenario, and the responsible-AI items in particular must avoid the saturated hiring/loan-approval settings the accessible source and Microsoft's own public material both use.

theme_definitions.F1: Workload identification — read a business situation and name the AI workload class or capability it belongs to, before any product or route is chosen
theme_definitions.F2: Output-granularity discrimination — the modality is obvious; the judgment is which technique or output granularity the requirement actually needs
theme_definitions.F3: Responsible-AI consideration — which principle a design decision discharges, which proposed control genuinely serves it, and which obligation governs when two principles pull against each other
theme_definitions.F4: Model and configuration choice — pick the model class, deployment option or inference parameter that produces the stated behaviour
theme_definitions.F5: Implementation-route selection — two supported Foundry routes reach the same outcome (multimodal model vs dedicated tool, portal vs SDK, purpose-built capability vs prompting a general model); a stated constraint decides
theme_definitions.F6: Build order and composition — what has to exist before what: deploy before invoke, recognise before analyse, classify before extract, and how a capability is composed into an agent
theme_definitions.F7: Autonomy tier — a model answering from a prompt, an agent that calls tools, or an agent grounded in a knowledge base: the rung the requirement actually needs, neither over- nor under-reached
theme_definitions.F8: Prompt and grounding craft — making a deployed model behave: what belongs in the system prompt, when examples or step-by-step reasoning are the right correction, and when an answer must be traceable to source content
